judgment_calls: SUPERSEDED by the 2026-08-21 repair: `testPrompts` bounds are no longer '1-20 entries, ≤4000 chars each' — that shape directly contradicted D1.2's closed-scenario contract and the track's no-raw-prompt rule. Replaced with a closed-membership check against `tool_test_scenarios.ts` (shared with D1.2), exactly 2-3 unique entries, no length bound needed since an identifier's shape is fixed and enumerable.

Check ORDER inside `validateToolInstallChange` (post-repair): required-4-fields → toolName safety → packageSource safety → installMethod closed-set → evidenceBundle presence/shape → testPrompts closed-scenario shape/bounds → agentConfigId existence → target ref/hash fabrication check. The toolName/packageSource safety checks were inserted right after the presence check and before installMethod, since a proposal with an unsafe identifier should never be considered 'well-formed enough' to reach the sandbox-relevant checks; this does not change any pre-existing test's expected reason substring (all pre-repair fixtures use safe `example-tool`/`npm:example-tool` values).

Production install-method registry (`npm install`, `pip install`) intentionally excludes `tool_sandbox_vetter.ts`'s `local-script` TEST-ONLY escape hatch, per that module's own doc comment forward-referencing 'the production proposal validator in D1.3'.

No raw-prompt-persistence check beyond the validator's own reason strings: this module performs no database write and no console/logger call of any kind, so there is no additional persistence/logging surface to test directly — the invariant is upheld structurally (there is no longer any field capable of carrying prompt text at all, only closed scenario identifiers).
